code:
a = np.ones((3, 4))
b = np.array([1, 2, 3, 4])  # (4,)
(a + b).shape
# (3, 4) -- b stretches over
#            every row, no copy
caption: Compare shapes from the trailing dimension; 1 stretches to match.

code:
returns = np.random.normal(
    0, 0.02, size=(250, 5))
mu = returns.mean(axis=0)   # (5,)
sd = returns.std(axis=0)    # (5,)
z = (returns - mu) / sd     # broadcasts
caption: No loop over the 5 assets -- the (5,) stats broadcast across 250 rows.

eyebrow: Strides: bytes to the next element
code:
m = np.arange(6).reshape(2, 3)
m.strides        # (24, 8)
m.T.strides      # (8, 24)
# .T swaps strides -- same memory,
# zero data copied
caption: Transposing is instant: it's a view with new metadata, not new data.

code:
arr = np.arange(10)
sl = arr[2:5]          # view
np.shares_memory(arr, sl)   # True

fancy = arr[[2, 3, 4]]      # copy
np.shares_memory(arr, fancy) # False
caption: Slices share memory; fancy indexing (list/boolean) always copies.
